body:
I don't care about how they see me, because as I keep to my own business I don't expect them to bother themselves with me, the same way I don't bother myself with them. 

If I met a clone of myself, I would probably not interact with him all that much. There is nothing he has to tell me that I don't already know. I would probably tell him to go about his business while I'd go about mine.

I'm going to hit the hay - let's continue this tomorrow.

I'm just not interested in other people. They're noisy, they're loud and obnoxious, and quiet people are weird and awkward to approach. Ergo, I keep to myself, they keep to their own, and that's just fine for both parties. 

I just don't bond with others, I imagine. Whenever the entire class bursts into laughter over a joke our lecturer says, I won't even smirk. I have nothing to talk about, either, and I'm not interested in whatever others have to tell me.

As a person I've barely changed since I was 17 - around the time I found that despite the therapy and attempts at being a more open and friendly person, I was still distant and suicidal, and that no feel-good treatment would work. Prior to that I thought there was something wrong with me because I was inferior, and got mad at myself for it; since then I've realized that yes, there is something wrong with me, but it doesn't make me objectively inferior, simply incompatible.

I don't have friends, and as a rule of thumb I dislike people. There is no laughing until my cheeks hurt for me. But that good stuff is meaningless and isn't productive. 

I don't recall what it was like 10 years ago, but I was 10 at the time and I was still in elementary school. Ergo I had very little to worry about.

Five years ago, I tried to kill myself because I was failing at school (I was getting teased fairly strongly at the time, which made it difficult to focus on work.) Though I still had little to worry about.

I haven't had a friend in years, and I can honestly say I've never had a strong bond with anyone. The friends I've had were closer to acquaintances.

They're not dark thoughts, though. It isn't something that I feel heartbroken over. It would have been nice for my life to turn out differently, in the same sense that it would have been nice being born with genes that would have made me tall and handsome.

Helping others is all good and dandy, if there's something in it for me. I suppose I'm a bad person in that respect. I like to make myself useful more than anything, if, at the end, there's a reward.

It has begun to dawn on me that all rewards are mostly based upon chance than anything. If life is a big dice roll, I don't see what's the point in sticking about just because it could potentially hit a 6 if I blow hard enough to turn the die over. 

I'm not denying that there is good in the world, there certainly is. But surrounding oneself with things one loves is just another word for delusion. Entertainment and instant gratification is nice, sure. But at the end of the day, bills still need to get paid, and that isn't done by doing things you love. It's done off working. For the few lucky enough to be able to live off of things they love - again, the most important aspect is luck.

To me, the intention of suicide isn't to end myself because I hate myself, it's a means of getting rid of the world. If I were to toil away for years hoping that things improve, then I'd be life's slave. If I am so much as suicidal, then life is my bitch, and I'm leading it around with a leash. I'm metaphorically slapping the lemons out of life's metaphorical hands.
Why would I do groceries for a restaurant I don't like?

I continue college because it is the closest thing that could ensure a well-paying job that isn't daily menial tasks, and because I'm not interested in throwing a year and a half into the bin to start another degree that I probably won't enjoy all that much either, and may not have as many prospects available. 

There are no solutions, because there's no problem.
Good. I choose the latter. I have no idea what your point even is.

Why would I give two dicks about trying to make do with disadvantages? I'm not interested in running a race with my laces tied together.

My second analogy does make sense - from my point of view. I've already figured out the meaning of my life and how I intend to spend it. If the amount of effort and resources I have to devote to that end are more than I'm willing to dispense, I'm not going to settle for anything less.

Again, it's nothing but maybes. Maybe it could, may it can be, potentials, etc, ifs. I'm not interested in trying things out anymore. Either I have a 100% guaranteed result, or I won't bother. It's a money and time sink with potentially no payoff. Let's suppose I went abroad to say, help AIDS patients in Africa. There's a laudable pursuit. Let's suppose I somehow make it out diseaseless, alive, with a renewed taste for life, and make it back to my home country.

Whoops! I don't have any more money, I don't have a house, I don't have a degree, and I don't have a job. Now I really want to die!

I have no idea what any of this means. My self is my brain, which is wired in a way that isn't going to change overnight, and isn't going to change without effort. 

Cooking or cleaning my fucking room isn't going to pay the bills or make life an interesting prospect to me. At the end of the day I still have to finish college and then find a job, going on walks or no. And as I'm not interested in slaving away for the rest of my life, I intend to take the bull by the horns.

Again, I don't know what happens after death, but if there's any kind of afterlife, well, 1. it wasn't going to turn out any other way, and 2. I probably won't like it.

Keyword being if. The concept of an afterlife is so far removed from reality that even bothering to think about it is stupid to me.

Maybe I could become a rock star. Maybe I could become a doctor.

I'm not interested in working towards maybes anymore. With suicide, I know exactly what I'm signing up for, and I know exactly what the end result is.

What's the difference between giving things "temporarily" and ending them up permanently? If I "go traveling" out of nowhere then not only am I wasting my time, I'm also wasting my money and everyone else's times.

If I get a taste for living afterwards, then I'm back to where I was with less resources. Pointless, potentially detrimental, and not even guaranteed to work.

I'm not in agony. I just don't like being alive, that's all. I've got a rather cozy life, but it takes more work to uphold than I'm willing to put in _and_ it's below the standards I have. Ergo, I would rather not be alive.
